name: GoliathApp
tagline: General-purpose enterprise platform for access control, workflows, and distributed workers.
description: GoliathApp is a general-purpose enterprise platform meant to be extended by specialized applications. Role-based access control and a database-backed workflow engine sit at the core. Applications define actions that implement workflows, and the platform enrolls and dispatches the distributed workers that run them. It has no upstream product dependency.

features.title: Role-based access control
features.description: Users, groups, roles, permissions, scopes, and sessions live in the RBAC schema. Portal procedures administer grants, invitations, and sessions.

features.title: Workflow engine
features.description: PostgreSQL runs workflow graphs: sequences, branches, loops, foreach, and events. Workers lease action nodes and the engine continues from result codes.

features.title: User-defined actions
features.description: Actions are data. Each action names a capability and input and output types. A specialized application supplies the handler that performs the action.

features.title: Workflow compiler
features.description: A DomainProgram document lowers to a workflow graph the engine can store and run. Control flow and action steps stay in the program, not in engine code.

features.title: Distributed workers
features.description: Workers enroll through the gateway from a preregistered address, then claim, heartbeat, and submit over REST. Capability lists, concurrency, and affinity decide which worker receives a task.

features.title: Pipeline profiles
features.description: Profile and procedure documents flatten into scope flags that workflow branches read. An application can ship its own profiles on top of the same resolver.

features.title: Release-time schema apply
features.description: The PostgreSQL scripts apply in a fixed order and can be applied again to a database that already has the objects. An application release runs that list once.

features.title: Semantic read layer
features.description: Portal registry tables and portal.sp_run_semantic_request expose customer-facing entities and saved queries. The goliath_portal role, goliath_app.portal.PortalClient, and optional Exograph GraphQL/MCP (goliath-exo) call stored procedures only.

features.title: Generic operator editors
features.description: The signed-in platform host at app.goliathresearch.com presents Meta-driven record grids (Add, View, Edit), a typed property grid, and a generic tree editor. Operators never type JSON. Child applications seed classes, data, and programs and inherit the same editors.

features.title: Typed config documents and site parameters
features.description: A child application registers the catalog data type of its site and pipeline-profile documents. The generic inspector edits them field by field. portal.fn_published_site_document returns a published site document for workers without interpreting keys.

features.title: Workflow designer and server-side compile
features.description: Operators edit versioned workflow graphs and DomainProgram steps in the portal. Compile and publish runs the platform's generic compiler on the server and creates an inactive workflow version.

features.title: Actions as class methods
features.description: Every action is a method on exactly one owning Meta class. The platform derives typed parameters from the action's input schema and checks that each catalog action has one owner.

features.title: Catalogs as Meta classes
features.description: Thirty-eight semantic, workflow, and cfg catalog kinds are projected as Meta classes. Meta is authoritative; the tables stay as the indexed read surface. A verifier checks that the two sides agree.
